scoped_clause_excerpts.text: [F1] Parabolic objects and Serre closure ([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]): finite Levi simples $E(\lambda)$ are inflated with radical acting by zero; $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_B E(\lambda)$ has simple head $L(\lambda)$ and lies in the Serre subcategory $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; the ordinary Verma surjects onto it. Duality preserves the subcategory and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ embeds in the ordinary dual Verma.

1.1 **Simples and standards.** By [F1], $\mathfrak p$-dominant highest weights are exactly the simple labels in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Their generalized standards are quotients of the ordinary Vermas with the same one-dimensional highest-weight space and simple head. They have finite length by [F2], and their weights, and hence highest weights of composition factors, lie in $\lambda-Q^+$ by [F3]. For any parabolic quotient of the ordinary Verma, the image of its highest vector is killed by the full positive nilpotent algebra. Its finite Levi span is the cyclic highest-weight simple $E(\lambda)$ by complete reducibility, and the radical kills that span since it kills the highest vector and is Levi-stable. The induction universal property therefore factors the quotient map through $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$. This proves the largest-quotient assertion locally. This proves parts (1) and (2). [F1, F2, F3, F4]

exact_native_before_affected_clauses.text: 1.1 **Simples and standards.** By [F1], Levi-dominant integral highest weights are exactly the simple labels in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Their generalized standards are quotients of the ordinary Vermas with the same one-dimensional highest-weight space and simple head. They have finite length by [F2], and their weights, and hence highest weights of composition factors, lie in $\lambda-Q^+$ by [F3]. For any parabolic quotient of the ordinary Verma, the image of its highest vector is killed by the full positive nilpotent algebra. Its finite Levi span is the cyclic highest-weight simple $E(\lambda)$ by complete reducibility, and the radical kills that span since it kills the highest vector and is Levi-stable. The induction universal property therefore factors the quotient map through $\Delta_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$. This proves the largest-quotient assertion locally. This proves parts (1) and (2). [F1, F2, F3, F4]

5.1 **Free finite rank gives generalized-standard flags.** Let $R$ be one of these parabolic $\mathfrak g$-modules, graded free of finite $N$-rank. Within its fixed $\zeta$-eigenvalue coset its degrees are bounded above and its components finite dimensional. Let $a$ be its highest occupied degree. The finite Levi module $R_a$ is semisimple and the positive radical kills it, as it raises degree. A homogeneous free basis shows that all its degree-$a$ basis vectors are part of an $N$-basis, so the induction map $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_B R_a=N\otimes R_a\to R$ is injective and its quotient is again graded free, with those finitely many generators removed. Decomposing $R_a$ into finite Levi simples gives an actual submodule that is a finite sum of generalized standards. Repeating on the quotient terminates since each step reduces the finite $N$-rank. All subobjects and quotients lie in the selected central summand; hence their simple Levi labels are the allowed labels there. This proves that every projective cover, and therefore every finite sum and summand of them, has a finite generalized-standard flag. The grading is only the actual semisimple $\zeta$-action, shifted on its coset; it is not a Koszul assumption. This proves the flag part of (4). [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 3.1, step 4.1, induction]

scoped_clause_excerpts.text: 1.1 Here is the ambient category used for the truncated assertions. For a deformation algebra $T$, its objects are finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes T$-modules which are direct sums of relative weight spaces $N^\xi=\{n:hn=(\xi(h)+\tau(h))n\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\}$, have finite $T$-modules as weight spaces, and have weights in a finite union of downward root cones. Morphisms preserve those weight spaces. The full subcategory $\mathcal O_T^{\le\Lambda}$ has weights $\xi\le\Lambda$ in one root-lattice coset; for a finite union of cosets use one bound in each coset. Kernels and cokernels remain in this category, as do extensions whose middle terms are relative-weight modules: weight decomposition makes weight spaces exact, the enveloping algebra over Noetherian $R$ is Noetherian by PBW, and positive-root action is locally nilpotent because only finitely many weights above a fixed weight occur. For arbitrary $R'$ the representing construction below uses the analogous category of relative weight modules, without requiring kernels of finitely generated objects to be finitely generated. Thus every projectivity/base-change assertion has a specified ambient category, distinct from the additive tensor family. [F1, algebra]

[F4] Crystal tensor rule ([[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]]): the tensor product of crystal lattices is a crystal lattice with residue basis the tensor classes $b\otimes b'$.

3.2 **The corrected tensor global vectors.** Within the finite raw-basis closure proved in step 1.1, or the separately supplied bounded ordered interval, apply the semilinear correction algorithm of [F2]: in each such finite transfer interval solve $g_t=e_t+\sum_{s>t}a_{ts}e_s$ with $a_{ts}\in q\mathbb Z[q]$ for the bar-fixed lift of the raw vector $e_t$. scoped_clause_excerpts.text: [F5] The ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig triangular construction over a finite Bruhat ideal, with bar-duality matrix $R$ satisfying $\bar RR=I$, diagonal one and lower-triangular support, produces the unique bar-fixed elements with the prescribed triangular support and shows they form a basis ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], step 1.1 of its proof).

1.1 **The coefficient matrices.** Define $r_{x,y}\in A$ for $x,y\in{}^JW$ by $\overline{m_y}=\sum_{x\le y}r_{x,y}m_x$, so $r_{x,y}=a_{x,y}$ for $x<y$, $r_{y,y}=1$, and $r_{x,y}=0$ when $x\not\le y$; define $s_{x,y}$ analogously from $\overline{n_y}=\sum_{x\le y}s_{x,y}n_x$. Applying bar to $\overline{m_y}=\sum_{x\le y}r_{x,y}m_x$ and using $\overline{\overline{m_y}}=m_y$ gives $m_y=\sum_{x\le y}\overline{r_{x,y}}\,\overline{m_x}=\sum_{x'\le y}\bigl(\sum_{x:x'\le x\le y}\overline{r_{x,y}}r_{x',x}\bigr)m_{x'}$; by [F1] the coefficient of $m_{x'}$ is $\delta_{x',y}$, that is, $R\bar R=I$ for the unitriangular matrix $R=(r_{x,y})$. A finite unitriangular matrix is invertible, so also $\bar RR=I$; the same identities hold for $S=(s_{x,y})$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 **Construction of the coefficients.** Fix $w\in{}^JW$ and increase $d=\ell(w)-\ell(x)$ over the finite lower ideal $I_w=\{x\in{}^JW:x\le w\}$ of [F3], starting with $c_{w,w}=1$. Suppose $x<w$ and $c_{y,w}$ has been constructed for every $y\in I_w$ with $x<y\le w$, satisfying $c_{y,w}=\sum_{y\le z\le w}r_{y,z}\overline{c_{z,w}}$; note that all cited labels lie in $I_w$. Put $a_x:=\sum_{x<y\le w}r_{x,y}\overline{c_{y,w}}$. Then $\overline{a_x}=\sum_{x<y\le w}\overline{r_{x,y}}c_{y,w}=\sum_{x<y\le z\le w}\overline{r_{x,y}}r_{y,z}\overline{c_{z,w}}=-\sum_{x<z\le w}r_{x,z}\overline{c_{z,w}}=-a_x$, where the middle equality substitutes the induction equations and the third uses $\bar RR=I$ from step 1.1: the sum over $x\le y\le z$ is zero for $x<z$, and its omitted diagonal term is $\overline{r_{x,x}}r_{x,z}=r_{x,z}$. Write $a_x=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\gamma_mv^m$; anti-invariance under $v\mapsto v^{-1}$ gives $\gamma_{-m}=-\gamma_m$, hence $\gamma_0=0$. Define $c_{x,w}:=\sum_{m>0}\gamma_mv^m$, so $c_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ and $c_{x,w}-\overline{c_{x,w}}=a_x$. The induction is finite and uses no choice principle. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Bar invariance and the coefficient equations.** Set $C_w:=\sum_{y\in I_w}c_{y,w}m_y$. The coefficient of $m_x$ in $\overline{C_w}$ is $\sum_{x\le y\le w}r_{x,y}\overline{c_{y,w}}$. For $x=w$ this is $\overline{c_{w,w}}=1=c_{w,w}$; for $x<w$ it is $\overline{c_{x,w}}+a_x=c_{x,w}$ by step 2.1, and for $x\notin I_w$ the support of $r_{x,y}$ makes the coefficient zero ($x\le y\le w$ would put $x\in I_w$). Hence $\overline{C_w}=C_w$ and the coefficient equation $c_{x,w}=\sum_{x\le y\le w}r_{x,y}\overline{c_{y,w}}$ holds for every $x\le w\in{}^JW$; this proves the existence, the bar invariance and the triangular support $C_w\in m_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]m_y$ of (i),(ii). Repeating the identical construction with the matrix $S$ in place of $R$ produces $D_w\in n_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]n_y$ with $\overline{D_w}=D_w$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

Comparing this equality with the sum over $C$ forces $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_W(Q(C),L_W(D))=\delta_{CD}$ for every summand with $m_C>0$. Thus each $Q(A)$ is the genuine projective cover of $L_W(A)$.
